question: The number of atoms in exactly 12 g of carbon-12 is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Avogadro's constant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Avogadro's constant is the number of atoms, molecules, or particles in one mole of a substance.
 
• It is defined as exactly 6.02214076 × 10^23 entities per mole.
 
• This constant is named after the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro.
 
• It plays a fundamental role in the field of chemistry and physics, particularly in the context of the mole concept and the calculation of the amount of substance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Faraday's Constant**

 
 
• Faraday's constant represents the electric charge per mole of electrons.
 
• It is approximately equal to 96485 coulombs per mole.
 
• This constant is used in electrochemistry to relate the amount of substance undergoing oxidation or reduction at an electrode to the quantity of electric charge passed through the substance.
 
 
 
• **Rydberg Constant**
 
 
• The Rydberg constant is associated with the wavelengths of spectral lines of hydrogen.
 
• It is used in atomic physics to describe the wavelengths of photons emitted during electron transitions between energy levels in an atom.
 
• The value of the Rydberg constant is approximately 1.097 × 10⁷ m^-1.
 
 
 
• **Planck's Constant**
 
 
• Planck's constant is a fundamental constant in quantum mechanics.
 
• It relates the energy of a photon to the frequency of its associated electromagnetic wave.
 
• The value of Planck's constant is approximately 6.626 × 10^-34 joule-seconds.
 
• This constant is central to the theory of quantum mechanics and helps to explain phenomena like the photoelectric effect.
